land.text: the Magadhan empire of the Nandas, which absorbed the Gangetic janapadas: 'The Nandas usurped the throne of Shishunaga dynasty c. 345 BCE, thus founding the Nanda Empire'; west edge as in nanda-empire (the Beas: 'beyond which the Nanda territory was located'), so Cliopatria's Sind and Baluchistan cells are left out (reviewer sa-01-d)

successors.note: The page's infobox 'Succeeded by' names the Nanda Empire. The association has no territory of its own; the land of the member states is handed over in their own dossiers.

land.text: 'Kamboja and Gandhara formed the twentieth and richest satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire'

successors.note: The page's infobox 'Succeeded by' also names the Achaemenid Empire; the conquest came in the reign of Cyrus II (558-530 BCE), long before 345, so this is a hand-over of two members, not of the association. Dated in janapada-of-gandhara and janapada-of-kamboja.

correction.text: the same 20-cell disc (5,163.5 km2) is Cliopatria's Janapada of Vajji shape (-600..-481): the Vajjika League 'bounded to the north, east, south, and west, respectively, by the Himālaya mountains, and the Mahānanda, Gaṅgā, and Sadānirā rivers', held until Ajātasattu managed 'to finally defeat the Vajjika League by 468 BCE and annex its territories'; the years -480..-468 belong to janapada-of-vajji, and from 468 the land is Magadha's (magadha-haryanka-dynasty), so nothing is drawn under this slug

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 'Mahajanapadas' row (-480..-451) is not a state: the Mahajanapadas page defines them as 'sixteen kingdoms and aristocratic republics', an association, and gives no area. The shape is cell for cell the Janapada of Vajji disc (data/shapes.csv: same area 5163.5, same bbox 85.3485,26.3222,86.3877,27.0938; the gazetteer resolves both to the same 20 cells), carried on under the umbrella's name after the Vajji row stops in -481. The Vajjika League page has the war declared in 484 BCE and the league beaten and annexed 'by 468 BCE' (infobox 'c. 468 BCE'), so the disc is Vajji's to 468 and Magadha's after; -467..-451 should show nothing of this row. The Mahajanapadas page is silent on Vajji's fate and gives no infobox area to compare.

region.text: the sixteen kingdoms and aristocratic republics of north India, as Cliopatria's umbrella entity draws them in 600 BCE

ledger.note: 600 BCE: the sixteen Mahajanapadas stand in the Iron Age north. The page says they 'existed in ancient India from the sixth to fourth centuries BCE' and gives no founding year, so -600 is the century's start (the Cliopatria umbrella '(Mahajanapadas)' also starts in -600). An association, never drawn as territory.

region.text: what remained of the sixteen states in Cliopatria's last umbrella shape, now inside Magadha's empire

ledger.note: 345 BCE: the Nandas take the Magadhan throne and the old order ends. 'The Nandas usurped the throne of Shishunaga dynasty c. 345 BCE, thus founding the Nanda Empire.' The infobox lists the Nanda Empire (and the Achaemenid Empire) as 'Succeeded by'. The page does not say the Mahajanapadas ended in 345; it says they lasted to the fourth century BCE, so the year is the Nanda founding date and the span end is my reading.

wars.name: Ajatashatru's war on the Vajjika League

zones.text: the Vajjika League's country, annexed 'including Licchavi, Videha, and Nāya'

wars.outcome: Magadha won: Ajātasattu 'declared war on the Vajjika League in 484 BCE' and needed diplomacy and intrigue 'to finally defeat the Vajjika League by 468 BCE and annex its territories'; the Mallakas also became part of his empire with limited autonomy.
wars.note: This is the war that ends the one real state behind Cliopatria's 'Mahajanapadas' disc. The contest and the hand-over are recorded in janapada-of-vajji and magadha-haryanka-dynasty, not here.

certainty.note: An association of sixteen states with no frontier of its own; each member's border is soft and is judged in its own dossier. The one Cliopatria shape under this slug is a mislabelled Vajji disc.

sources.title: Mahajanapadas
sources.note: Definition ('sixteen kingdoms and aristocratic republics ... from the sixth to fourth centuries BCE'), infobox successors (Nanda and Achaemenid empires), 'The Nandas usurped the throne ... c. 345 BCE', the Achaemenid satrapy of Kamboja and Gandhara; no area figure.

sources.title: Vajjika League
sources.note: Ajatashatru's war from 484 BCE and the annexation 'by 468 BCE' (infobox c. 468 BCE): the fate of the disc that Cliopatria labels Mahajanapadas.

notes: Budget: two pages. TYPE: written as an umbrella (rule 4: associations are never territory), although Cliopatria files 'Mahajanapadas' as an ordinary polity row (not parenthesised) with a Wikidata id (Q846025) shared with the umbrella entity '(Mahajanapadas)' (slug rel-mahajanapadas, -600..-351, 7 shapes). If the orchestrator prefers one entity, merge this dossier into rel-mahajanapadas; it adds nothing the umbrella does not already say except the verdict on the -480 shape. THE SHAPE: mahajanapadas_-480 (-480..-451, 5,163.5 km2) is the Janapada of Vajji disc (same cells), continued after the Vajji row stops in -481; verdict wrong; the sibling dossiers janapada-of-vajji (keyframe -480..-468) and magadha-haryanka-dynasty (gain at 468) already carry the land, so nothing is lost by dropping this row. Do not draw it as territory. PAGES: the Mahajanapadas page in this copy lacks the list of sixteen (it says the Anguttara Nikaya 'gives a list of sixteen great states' but the list is missing from the text I received) and has no section headings; the member dossiers are in the other sa-01 parts. DATES: -600 start and -345 end are mine from 'sixth to fourth centuries BCE' and the Nanda infobox; Cliopatria's umbrella runs -600..-351. The infobox 'Preceded by' lists the Painted Grey Ware culture, the Vedic period, the Janapadas and the Kuru kingdom, none of which is a dossier of this batch (sa-01-x covers the pre-600 cultures); predecessors is therefore empty. Gazetteer: no new names needed.
